## Experiment and agent architecture

This run has **`r nrow(scenarios)` scenarios** and **`r 3*nrow(scenarios)` source
designs**: **`r sum(usage$origin == "imported")` imported** from the revised run
and **`r sum(usage$origin == "generated")` newly generated**. One simulation
iteration is used per scenario, with no additional validation draws. The grid
includes planning targets **0.2, 0.6, and 0.9**. Each setting contains three
independent studies with independent exposed/control samples. A measurement's
effect can be present in zero, one, two, or three studies, with probabilities
60%, 15%, 15%, and 10%. The sample-size planning formula is unchanged.

Each PydanticAI agent observes its own study, explores using R, and freezes an
analysis, directional hypotheses, and scientific explanation. Histories and
workspaces are separate. Docker isolates R execution from credentials, truth,
generator code, other workspaces, and the network. All three source attempts
finish before selection. Imported designs retain their original bytes and are
rechecked offline on their own source data; their historical usage is separate
from this run's new API usage. Agent prompts, model, and reference context are unchanged.

## Pooled algorithm selection

For each held-out target, pool the other two studies' exposed samples and,
separately, their controls. Apply those two studies' frozen algorithms to this
same pooled pair at **0.05/3**. Choose the algorithm with more unique measurement
discoveries, breaking ties by the smaller source-agent index. Apply it unchanged
to the held-out study at **0.05/3** in a fresh container. Failed candidates are
excluded and flagged; a target fails if both candidates fail. Target observations
and simulation truth play no part in selection, and no results return to agents.

These pooled discovery counts are exploratory selection scores: each candidate
was designed using part of the pooled data. Confirmed outcomes come only from
the held-out target. `agent_pooled_select` is the new procedure; `agent_cycle` is
the original 1→2, 2→3, 3→1 procedure using the same frozen designs.

Full Welch and known-variance z baselines test both directions for every
measurement separately in each study. They use Holm for FWER, and BH/BY variants
for FDR, at the same 0.05/3 level. The oracle z baseline knows variance information
withheld from agents.

## Primary measure: study-count recovery

For each measurement h, let r_h be the number of studies with a true nonzero
effect, and let rhat_h be the number of studies reporting a discovery. Each study
counts at most once, even if both directions are rejected. For r_h > 0:

$$
U_h = \begin{cases}
\widehat r_h/r_h, & \widehat r_h \le r_h,\\
0, & \widehat r_h > r_h.
\end{cases}
$$

The scenario score is the **unweighted average over measurements with r_h > 0**.
If there are three true study effects, claiming one, two, or three earns 1/3,
2/3, or 1. If there are two and three are claimed, credit is zero. All-null
measurements are excluded from this average; discoveries for them and other
overclaims are reported separately. A missing target makes the score incomplete.

This is a **count-only score**: it can award credit even when the particular
studies or directions are wrong. Directional false discoveries, FDP, and the
original directional power therefore remain separate secondary outcomes.

```{r recovery}
value <- function(id,method) {
  x <- counts$study_count_recovery[counts$scenario==id & counts$method==method]
  if(length(x)==1L) x else NA_real_
}
table <- do.call(rbind,lapply(seq_len(nrow(scenarios)),function(i) {
  s <- scenarios[i,]; suffix <- if(s$criterion=="FDR") "_bh" else ""
  data.frame(Scenario=s$id, `Selected agents`=value(s$id,"agent_pooled_select"),
    `Cyclic agents`=value(s$id,"agent_cycle"), `Welch Holm/BH`=value(s$id,paste0("welch",suffix)),
    `Welch BY`=if(s$criterion=="FDR") value(s$id,"welch_by") else NA_real_,
    `Oracle Holm/BH`=value(s$id,paste0("oracle_variance_z",suffix)),check.names=FALSE)
}))
knitr::kable(table, digits = 4)
```

```{r recovery-plot, out.width='100%'}
if (file.exists("study-count-recovery.png")) knitr::include_graphics("study-count-recovery.png")
```

## Errors and interpretation

```{r errors}
selected <- scores[scores$method=="agent_pooled_select",]
knitr::kable(selected[,intersect(c("scenario","complete","overclaimed_measurements",
  "all_null_discoveries","false","realized_fdp","power"),names(selected))],digits=4)
```

The error table above describes the selected agents. Full results for every
method, including the oracle BY variant, are in the linked CSV tables and full
report. `false` counts directional false claims; `power` is the original
directional power and is distinct from study-count recovery.

These are realized outcomes from one iteration, not estimates of long-run FWER
or FDR. Count recovery is a utility measure, not an error-control guarantee.
Successful contract checks establish executable structure, not statistical
validity. The frozen algorithms retain their modeling and multiplicity assumptions.

```{r comparison, results='asis'}
primary <- counts[counts$method == "agent_pooled_select", ]
cycle <- counts[counts$method == "agent_cycle", ]
cycle <- cycle[match(primary$scenario, cycle$scenario), ]
valid <- is.finite(primary$study_count_recovery) & is.finite(cycle$study_count_recovery)
cat(sprintf("Pooled selection improved recovery over the cyclic agents in **%d of %d comparable scenarios**, tied in **%d**, and was lower in **%d**.\n\n",
  sum(primary$study_count_recovery[valid] > cycle$study_count_recovery[valid]), sum(valid),
  sum(primary$study_count_recovery[valid] == cycle$study_count_recovery[valid]),
  sum(primary$study_count_recovery[valid] < cycle$study_count_recovery[valid])))
welch <- vapply(primary$scenario,function(id) {
  criterion <- scenarios$criterion[match(id,scenarios$id)]
  value(id,if(criterion=="FDR") "welch_bh" else "welch")
},numeric(1))
valid <- is.finite(primary$study_count_recovery) & is.finite(welch)
cat(sprintf("Against full Welch with the matching primary correction (Holm or BH), pooled selection was higher in **%d**, tied in **%d**, and lower in **%d** scenarios.\n\n",
  sum(primary$study_count_recovery[valid] > welch[valid]),
  sum(primary$study_count_recovery[valid] == welch[valid]),
  sum(primary$study_count_recovery[valid] < welch[valid])))
```

Selecting the algorithm with more pooled discoveries produced mixed held-out
results. A larger pooled count does not ensure better recovery in a different
study. These comparisons use the same frozen designs and observations; they do
not establish a reliable advantage from one simulation iteration.

## Sample sizes and execution

```{r planning}
knitr::kable(planning, digits = 5)
```

`n` is the sample size per exposed/control arm in each study; `c` is the planning
power target. It is distinct from the reported study-count recovery score.

```{r usage}
table <- data.frame(Measure=c("Imported designs","New designs","New physical API attempts",
  "New input tokens","New output tokens","New session time, minutes"),
  Value=c(sum(usage$origin=="imported"),sum(usage$origin=="generated"),sum(usage$api_attempts),
    sum(usage$input_tokens),sum(usage$output_tokens),sum(usage$seconds)/60))
knitr::kable(table,digits=2)
```

Imported rows show zero new usage and separate historical API attempts. Missing
usage in a failed session is not evidence of zero provider billing.

claimed counts, recovery credit, and overclaim indicators. Each agent's
`frozen/report.md` contains its recommendations and rationale; `frozen/analysis.R`
and `audit/exploration/` contain its final and exploratory code.
